findings.reason: The new branch at index.js:307-312 calls setArg(key, defaultValue(key)) and never looks at args[i+1]. The short-flag path at index.js:299-301 and the long-flag path at index.js:205-207 both take a following true/false, so `-0 false` behaves differently from `--print0 false`.
findings.claim: A single-digit boolean alias ignores an explicit true/false value after it, so `-0 false` sets print0 to true and puts 'false' in argv._.
findings.evidence: With arguments ['-0', 'false'] and options {alias: {0: 'print0'}, boolean: ['print0']}, the new branch calls setArg(key, defaultValue(key)), which supplies true, without inspecting or consuming the next token. The next iteration adds 'false' to argv._. Both existing long-option and short-option branches consume following true/false values, so '--print0 false' correctly disables the same option.

findings.reason: index.js:199-203 consumes any next arg matching `negative`, and nothing checks whether that digit is a boolean alias, so the claim holds. But giving a value-taking option a negative number is long-standing behaviour, and no story text says `-0` should win here, so whether this is a defect is unsettled. Lowered to low.
findings.claim: `--name -0` takes -0 as name's value even when 0 is a declared boolean alias.
findings.evidence: The new branch at index.js:307 runs only when `-0` is the current arg. The space-separated value lookahead at index.js:199-201 (`next.match(negative)`) and at index.js:293-294 consumes any next arg matching `negative` (`/^-([0-9]+...)$/`, line 56) as the value, without checking whether that digit is a declared boolean alias. The diff adds no test for `-0` after a value-taking flag.

findings.reason: eatArray at index.js:413/423 and eatNargs at index.js:388 accept any arg matching `negative`, so `--files a b -0` puts -0 into files. That matches the existing rule that arrays accept negative numbers, and the spec doesn't say which should win, so the code alone can't settle it. Lowered to low.
findings.claim: Array and nargs options swallow a following `-0` as a value instead of setting the boolean.
findings.evidence: eatArray breaks only when `/^-/.test(next) && !negative.test(next)` (index.js:413, 423), and eatNargs counts an arg as available when `!args[ii].match(/^-[^0-9]/) || args[ii].match(negative)` (index.js:388). Both treat `-0` as a value even when `checkAllAliases('0', flags.bools)` is true. The new feature therefore works only where the tests try it: standalone, or after a plain flag that already has its value.

findings.reason: index.js:309 checks only flags.bools, so a count-typed digit alias reaches argv._.push at index.js:320. The comment and tests scope the feature to boolean aliases, so whether counts were in scope can't be told without the story.
findings.claim: Single-digit count flags are not handled and still fall through to argv._.
findings.evidence: The new branch checks only `checkAllAliases(arg.slice(1), flags.bools)`. Unlike the neighbouring branches (e.g. lines 201-202), it does not also check `flags.counts`, so a count-typed digit alias goes to the `argv._.push(maybeCoerceNumber('_', arg))` fallback at line 320.

findings.reason: negative at index.js:56 matches every string that `/^-[0-9]$/` matches, so the line-308 check never changes the result. This is a readability point only.
findings.evidence: Line 307 tests `arg.match(/^-[0-9]$/)` and line 308 then tests `arg.match(negative)`, where `negative = /^-([0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?|\.[0-9]+)$/` (line 56) is a strict superset of the first pattern.

findings.reason: The second hunk of diff.patch removes the XXX comment, and index.js:356 still uses Object.keys(aliases).map(...). This is out-of-scope churn that drops a recorded follow-up, not a defect.
findings.claim: The diff deletes an unrelated node 6 `Object.values` TODO without doing the follow-up.
findings.evidence: diff.patch hunk @@ -347,7 +353,6 @@ deletes `// XXX Switch to [].concat(...Object.values(aliases)) once node.js 6 is dropped`, while line 356 still uses `Object.keys(aliases).map(k => aliases[k])`, the pattern the TODO asked to replace.
